behavior: Transactions CSV, the statement PDF and balance history stay bounded in memory, whatever a wallet receives
acceptance: The CSV and the statement read rows as they come instead of loading them all; the statement keeps only income lines.
A period with more than 10000 transactions answers 422 too_many_transactions, and the Export dialog says to pick a shorter period.
Balance history no longer loads every transfer row into memory.
With 100000 dust transfers, ten parallel exports stay far below the audit's 1.1 GB peak (the audit PoC as a test).
notes:
2026-10-19 review fail by subagent: Blocker:
1) apps/backend/api/openapi.yaml:2350: the Error schema's code enum lacks too_many_transactions. The new 422 responses (lines 898-902, 933-937) name that code, so the contract contradicts itself. A client or validator built from the spec rejects the response. Every other code in httpio/errors.go is in the enum (F240 added not_labelable the same way). Fix: add too_many_transactions to the enum.

Checked, OK:
- Balance history matches the old walk. least((block_time - start)/86400, days-1) gives the same day buckets: block_time >= start, so the bigint division is never negative and truncates like floor. Today's bucket has no end, as before. block_number <= r.block per token equals the old skip. Tokens without a wallet balance are ignored as before. The below-0 clamp and received/sent per day are unchanged. tokens has key (chain_id, contract), so the unnest join cannot double rows. Empty arrays encode as NULL, and unnest gives no rows.
- EachTransfer: LIMIT 10001. Exactly 10000 rows pass; the 10001st returns ErrTooMany before fn runs.
- CSV: header, formula guard and CRLF are unchanged. Content-Type and Content-Disposition are set only on success; errors stay JSON.
- Statement: lines come newest first, then slices.Reverse gives the old oldest-first order. The Unclassified count is unchanged.
- The DB connection is held only while rows are formatted in memory. The file and PDF go to the client after the connection is released. Acceptable.
- Web: responseHandler parses JSON on error, like the statement. Both downloads show the new line. Tests cover CSV and statement.
- No other HTTP reader loads every wallet transfer. Transfers is paged and SetLabel reads one transfer. The watcher's pending read is bounded by finality and is outside this task.

Ran:
- go test -count=1 ./internal/balance/ ./internal/activity/ ./internal/httpapi/tests/: all ok.
- npx vitest run src/features/transactions: 6/6 passed.
- New test on the base tree (git archive 6075d8e into scratch, since removed): it FAILS. 200 instead of 422; CSV 3544 MB, statement 2243 MB, history 29 MB.
- Latest docs/runs/F251-20261019T190035Z-*: all checks passed.

Minor:
(a) By design, 10001 dust transfers in one UTC day block that day's CSV and statement. No shorter period exists. The statement keeps only income lines, so it would stay bounded without the cap. Owner's call.
(b) No test at exactly 10000 vs 10001 rows. The code reads right.
(c) exports_bounded_test.go: the fake balance block is 100, so only 100 dust rows reach the history SUM. The test still fails on the old code.
(d) R-118 and the test comment say the audit measured 3 GB; the base run gives 3.5 GB. Accept 4 says 1.1 GB peak.
(e) docs/web/DESIGN.md (Export dialog errors) does not list the too-many line. R-118 covers it.
(f) The DB still joins and sorts every row in the period before LIMIT. Memory is bounded, but DB time still grows with dust.
